questions.question_text: During an assessment interview, the clinician asked a 23-year-old man questions such as, 'What did your mother say when your father said this to your brother?' . Which interview technique is used in this case?
questions.explanation: Circular questioning can be confusing and obstructive in eliciting information.

questions.question_text: During a therapy session of a family consisting of the couple, two daughters and a son, the son had been quiet and said very little, if anything. On the other hand, the couple and their daughters tended to fill the silence by saying almost anything, or having a silly laugh. The therapist then asked the couple, 'If your son spoke now what might he say?' . Which interview technique is used in this case?
questions.explanation: This type of question leads to an imaginative or unspoken response in the therapy sessions.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old man told his doctor that Jesus spoke to him whenever he started his motorbike and stopped talking to him whenever he switched the engine off. He found this very distressing and confusing, so could not use his motorbike to go to work. Which of the following explains this experience?
questions.explanation: Functional hallucination requires the presence of another real sensory modality.

questions.question_text: A 37-year-old single American man informed his doctor that, whenever he saw President Obama on television, he got sharp pains in his right leg. He was convinced that President Obama was controlling him through the television. Which of the following can explain this man's experience?
questions.explanation: This is a form of synaesthesia where a stimulus of one sensory modality produces a sensory experience in another.

questions.question_text: A 61-year-old business executive had an exploratory laparotomy 5 days ago. He told the nurses that he saw tiny pink elephants and white tigers dancing outside the windowsills. He has a history of alcohol dependence. Which of the following explains his experience?
questions.explanation: Lilliputian hallucinations are visual hallucinations where the person sees tiny people or objects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a closed question?

options.text: 'So, do I understand this correctly that … ?'
'What brought you to the emergency department today?'
'You were not sleeping at that time?'

questions.explanation: A closed question typically has a straightforward 'yes' or 'no' answer or a single word response.

questions.question_text: What does the three-stage command in the mini-mental state examination (MMSE) test?
questions.explanation: The three-stage command is used to assess language understanding.

questions.question_text: A 48-year-old married man was concerned that he might be developing Parkinson's disease. Which of the following clinical features is diagnostic?
questions.explanation: Facial hypomimia is a classic sign associated with Parkinson's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most appropriate and quickest assessment test for performance IQ?
questions.explanation: Raven's progressive matrices is a non-verbal test widely used for assessing performance IQ.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Addenbrooke's cognitive examination is correct?

options.text: Possible outcomes include delirium, dementia and depression with psychotic symptoms
Scores of < 82 predict dementia with 100% specificity
Scores of < 82 predict dementia with 100% sensitivity
Scores of < 90 predict dementia with 100% sensitivity
The MMSE should be conducted separately

correct_answer.text: Scores of < 82 predict dementia with 100% sensitivity

correct_answers.text: Scores of < 82 predict dementia with 100% sensitivity

questions.explanation: Scores of < 82 predict dementia with 100% sensitivity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is assessed by the clock-drawing test?
questions.explanation: The clock-drawing test is used to assess orientation to time and person.

questions.question_text: You are assessing the language function in a 50-year-old man with a history of cerebrovascular accident. He says 'litter for letter'. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: This is an example of phonemic paraphasia where words with similar sounds are substituted.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a non-verbal test for semantic memory?
questions.explanation: The cactus and camel test is designed to assess semantic memory non-verbally.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be assessed by the word stem completion task?
questions.explanation: The word stem completion task assesses priming, a type of implicit memory.

questions.question_text: Which of the following lobe functions is assessed by the Iowa gambling test assess?
questions.explanation: The Iowa gambling task primarily assesses decision-making capabilities linked to the frontal lobe.

questions.question_text: A 31-year-old man presented with a spinal injury. On examination, you diagnosed that he had spastic paralysis of the lower limbs. You tested his sensations and found that he had sensation above the umbilicus. Where is the spinal cord lesion?
questions.explanation: Sensations below T10 would be disrupted with an injury at this level.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is present in the Brown–Séquard syndrome with a right-sided lesion?

options.text: Left hemiplegia of the arm and leg
Loss of pain and temperature sensation on the left side
Loss of proprioception and vibration sense on the left side

correct_answer.text: Loss of pain and temperature sensation on the left side

correct_answers.text: Loss of pain and temperature sensation on the left side

questions.explanation: In Brown–Séquard syndrome, pain and temperature sensation are lost contralaterally due to a right-sided lesion.

questions.question_text: A 33-year-old man was hit on his head during a fight. He was suspected of having an extradural haematoma. Which of the following signs is the first indication of raised intracranial pressure causing compression of cranial nerve III?

options.text: Ipsilateral eyeball abducted and directed slightly inferiorly
Ipsilateral slowness of the pupillary response

correct_answer.text: Ipsilateral slowness of the pupillary response

correct_answers.text: Ipsilateral slowness of the pupillary response

questions.explanation: The first sign indicating raised intracranial pressure affecting cranial nerve III is ipsilateral slowness of the pupillary response to light.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old man diagnosed with hypothyroidism complained that he had an aching pain in his right hand with paraesthesia, occurring mainly at night. Which sign are you most likely to elicit?

options.text: Loss of pronation of the forearm
No sensory loss over the palm
Sensory loss over the little finger

questions.explanation: Wasting of the thenar muscles is indicative of carpal tunnel syndrome.

questions.question_text: A 70-year-old woman presented with hearing loss and tinnitus. Investigations led to a diagnosis of acoustic neuroma. You examine the patient's cranial nerves. What sign are you most likely to elicit?
questions.explanation: Facial weakness is common with acoustic neuroma due to cranial nerve involvement.

questions.question_text: You were called to assess an 83-year-old man who was found wandering by the police. During the MMSE, you asked him to remember three objects but he was unable to repeat them after 1 minute. Which type of memory deficit has been elicited?
questions.explanation: The patient's inability to recall the three objects indicates a deficit in working memory.

questions.question_text: A 79-year-old widow with Alzheimer's disease attended the day hospital regularly. She continued enjoying knitting, which she used to do before developing her condition. Which of her memories remains intact?
questions.explanation: Procedural memory, which includes skills such as knitting, often remains intact in dementia.

questions.question_text: A 31-year-old man was unconscious for 1 week after a road traffic accident. On examination, he had no memory for any events for a period of 2 weeks before the accident. What type of memory loss does this refer to?
questions.explanation: Retrograde memory loss refers to the inability to recall events that occurred before the injury.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old man with schizophrenia presented with complaints of visual hallucinations, restlessness and marked thirst. On examination, he was agitated and had a raised body temperature, dilated pupils, dry mouth and urinary retention. Which of the following is most likely to account for this clinical presentation?
questions.explanation: Antimuscarinic intoxication can present with these symptoms, including agitation and physiological changes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) scan reports is characteristic of Alzheimer's disease?

options.text: Increased perfusion in the frontal lobes
Increased perfusion in the lateral temporal lobes
Increased perfusion in the parietal lobes
Reduced perfusion in the occipital lobes
Reduced perfusion in the posterior temporal lobes

correct_answer.text: Reduced perfusion in the posterior temporal lobes

correct_answers.text: Reduced perfusion in the posterior temporal lobes

questions.explanation: Reduced perfusion in the posterior temporal lobes is a characteristic finding on SPECT in Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tests is used to assess executive function?
questions.explanation: Hayling's sentence completion test assesses executive function by evaluating response initiation and suppression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a specific test for frontal lobe dysfunction?
questions.explanation: The cognitive estimates test requires educated guesses and is indicative of frontal lobe functioning.

questions.question_text: Polymorphism of genes is associated with an increased risk of depression when exposed to psychosocial stressors. Which of the following is affected?
questions.explanation: Variation in the serotonin transporter gene is linked to mood disorders and the trait of neuroticism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder?

options.text: High levels of noradrenaline metabolites (3-methyl-4-hydrophenyl glycol)
Polymorphism in the dopamine D4 transporter gene

correct_answer.text: Polymorphism in the dopamine D4 transporter gene

correct_answers.text: Polymorphism in the dopamine D4 transporter gene

questions.explanation: Polymorphism in the dopamine D4 transporter gene has been linked to an increased likelihood of developing ADHD.

questions.question_text: An 82-year-old widow living with her son presented with the first onset of somatic and auditory hallucinations accompanied by persecutory delusions. Which of the following is a risk factor for this presentation?
questions.explanation: Impaired hearing can increase the risk of psychotic symptoms in older adults.

questions.question_text: The current evidence suggests that the risk of developing psychiatric illness is increased within 6 months of a significant life event. By what factor is this risk increased?
questions.explanation: Research indicates that the risk is increased by 2–7 times following significant life events.

questions.question_text: With what is HLA-DQB1-*0602 mainly associated?
questions.explanation: HLA-DQB1-*0602 is prominently linked with narcolepsy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following parts of the brain is likely to be involved in the difference between homosexual and heterosexual men?
questions.explanation: Research indicates structural differences in the hypothalamus between homosexual and heterosexual men.

questions.question_text: An 8-year-old girl frequently got into trouble at school because she disturbed the other pupils and could not sit still in the classroom. However, when she was alone with her tutor she worked well and productively. What is the most likely aetiology of this child's problem?
questions.explanation: Neurological dysfunction is a likely underlying cause of attention-related behaviors.

questions.question_text: With what is tuberous sclerosis most likely to be associated?
questions.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis has a strong association with autism spectrum disorders.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old female postgraduate student became extremely angry when her college thesis committee refused to approve her project. She claimed, 'They are just jealous of me because I will be the most brilliant scientist in the United Kingdom'. It has been observed that she has had such attitudes all her life. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The features of grandiosity and a need for admiration suggest narcissistic personality disorder.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old female nurse had recurrent intrusive thoughts of stabbing a patient with a hypodermic needle. She found the thoughts unpleasant, horrible and anxiety provoking, but was able to resist them. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The presence of intrusive thoughts that are resisted suggests obsessive–compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: A 26-year-old man liked wearing clothes of the opposite sex. He did not get any sexual gratification from the act but just enjoyed membership of the opposite sex. There was no desire for a sex change. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Dual-role transvestism involves wearing clothing of the opposite gender for social belonging without sexual gratification.

questions.question_text: An 18-year-old man presented with transient perceptual abnormalities and incongruent affect. He was noticed to be giggling to himself. There were affective changes and some evidence of a thought disorder. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Hebephrenic schizophrenia is characterized by disorganized behavior and affective abnormalities.

questions.question_text: According to the International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision (ICD-10), which of the following is a diagnostic criterion of paranoid personality disorder?

options.text: Being excessively sensitive to setbacks and rebuffs
Lack of desire for close friends or confiding relationships

correct_answer.text: Being excessively sensitive to setbacks and rebuffs

correct_answers.text: Being excessively sensitive to setbacks and rebuffs

questions.explanation: Excessive sensitivity to setbacks and rebuffs is a key feature of paranoid personality disorder.

questions.question_text: On which DSM-IV (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 4th edn) axis, is a medical condition coexisting with a mental disorder recorded?
questions.explanation: General medical conditions are recorded on Axis III, while clinical disorders are on Axis I.

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between the DSM-IV-TR and the ICD-10 criteria used for the diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder?
questions.explanation: The DSM-IV-TR specifies criteria for functional impairment, which are not included in ICD-10.

questions.question_text: According to the ICD-10 classification, onset of symptoms in post-traumatic stress disorder should be within a specified period of time. What is this duration?
questions.explanation: The ICD-10 requires that symptoms develop within 6 months of the traumatic event for PTSD diagnosis.

questions.question_text: Which publication of the ICD had included a section on mental disorders for the first time?
questions.explanation: ICD-6 was the first publication to include a section on mental disorders.

questions.question_text: You get a call from the duty physician about a 38-year-old man with bipolar affective disorder whose mental state had been stable on lithium. The duty physician would like to start him on a diuretic as soon as possible. Which of the following diuretics does not interfere with the serum concentration of lithium?
questions.explanation: Furosemide is a loop diuretic that generally does not affect lithium clearance.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man with a family history of diabetes mellitus presented with psychotic symptoms. Which of the following antipsychotics does not interfere with blood sugar?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride has been shown to have a lesser impact on blood glucose levels compared to the others listed.

questions.question_text: You get a call from the duty obstetrician about a 32-year-old woman who was 15 weeks' pregnant and her bipolar affective disorder was stabilised on lithium. Which of the following statements about use of lithium in pregnancy is correct?

options.text: Lithium is not excreted in breast milk.
Lithium use does not affect the fetus in the second trimester
Lithium use in the first trimester is associated with neural tube defects in the fetus
Serum lithium levels increase in the third trimester of pregnancy
Serum lithium levels increase in the immediate postpartum period

correct_answer.text: Serum lithium levels increase in the immediate postpartum period

correct_answers.text: Serum lithium levels increase in the immediate postpartum period

questions.explanation: Lithium use in the first trimester is associated with an increased risk of neural tube defects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following mood stabilisers has the best evidence for reducing the rates of completed suicides in bipolar affective disorder?
questions.explanation: Lithium has been shown to significantly reduce the risk of both attempted and completed suicides in bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: You review a 42-year-old man with a psychotic episode on the ward. He had been prescribed quetiapine since his admission last week. He went on leave and had a glass of grapefruit juice at home. How does grapefruit juice affect quetiapine metabolism?

options.text: Chemical components of grapefruit juice can free more quetiapine from protein-binding site
Grapefruit juice decreases the excretion of quetiapine
Grapefruit juice has no effect on quetiapine metabolism
Grapefruit juice irreversibly blocks intestinal cytochrome P450
Grapefruit juice reversibly blocks intestinal cytochrome P450

correct_answer.text: Grapefruit juice irreversibly blocks intestinal cytochrome P450

correct_answers.text: Grapefruit juice irreversibly blocks intestinal cytochrome P450

questions.explanation: Grapefruit juice irreversibly inhibits cytochrome P450 3A4, increasing the effects of medications metabolized by this pathway.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man wanted to stop smoking and therefore engaged himself in a therapy programme, where the act of smoking was paired with imagining a horrible taste. On every occasion thereafter, every time he got an urge to smoke, he imagined the horrible taste. This approach helped him to stop smoking. What technique has his therapist used to help him stop smoking?
questions.explanation: Covert sensitisation uses imagery to create negative associations with the undesired behavior.

questions.question_text: Systemic desensitisation is an application of classic conditioning. What is the principle involved?
questions.explanation: Systemic desensitisation combines reciprocal inhibition with graded exposure to the feared object.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about assimilation in Piaget's theory of cognitive development is correct?

options.text: It is a process through which a child interprets new experiences by incorporating them into an existing schema
It is a process by which the child modifies existing schema to incorporate new experiences
It leads to development of new schema

correct_answer.text: It is a process through which a child interprets new experiences by incorporating them into an existing schema

correct_answers.text: It is a process through which a child interprets new experiences by incorporating them into an existing schema

questions.explanation: Assimilation involves incorporating new experiences into existing schemas without changing the schemas.

questions.question_text: At what age does object permanence occur?
questions.explanation: Object permanence typically develops between 18 to 24 months of age according to Piaget.

questions.question_text: What do we call drawing inferences about the relationship between two things based on a single shared attribute? AI chose E
questions.explanation: Transductive reasoning involves inferring relationships based on a shared attribute without clear logic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs in the sensorimotor stage of Piaget's theory of cognitive development? AI chose D
questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage involves basic reflex actions and sensory experiences.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Piaget's stages of cognitive development is correct? AI chose C

options.text: In the sensorimotor stage, the child is egocentric
Lack of conservation is a feature of the formal operational stage
Logical reasoning is not present until the formal operational stage
Non-logical thought is a feature of children aged 7–11 years
The preoperational stage lasts for about 5 years

correct_answer.text: Non-logical thought is a feature of children aged 7–11 years

correct_answers.text: Non-logical thought is a feature of children aged 7–11 years

questions.explanation: Logical reasoning begins during the concrete operational stage, which follows the preoperational stage.

questions.question_text: Which of the behavioural theorists first described the concept of operant conditioning?
questions.explanation: B.F. Skinner is known for his work on operant conditioning, focusing on how rewards and punishments shape behavior.

questions.question_text: An 8-month-old girl enjoyed picking up toys and bringing them to her mouth. She was often seen sucking them. What phase of Freud's psychosexual development is she going through?
questions.explanation: The oral phase occurs from birth to around 18 months, focusing on oral activities such as sucking and biting.

questions.question_text: According to Freud, during psychosexual development a boy focuses his love on his mother. This can reach a stage where a boy becomes jealous of his father and wants to kill him. However, he cannot do this for fear of castration and so represses these urges as he moves to the next stage of development. Which of the following describes the boy's psychosocial development?
questions.explanation: The Oedipus complex describes a boy's feelings of desire for his mother and jealousy towards his father.

questions.question_text: A child copies a circle, uses basic grammatically correct sentences, shows cooperative play, has a fear of animals and the dark, and also has his own sexual identity. What is his age?
questions.explanation: A 3-year-old child can exhibit these developments in play and language skills.

questions.question_text: A 24-year-old man exhibited an outpouring of emotions during a lengthy discussion of childhood memories. He was often angry, rambled excessively, and was distressed and tearful. Which category of Mary Main's adult attachment interview is he representing?
questions.explanation: Preoccupied attachment is characterized by emotional responses and difficulty in maintaining a coherent narrative.

questions.question_text: A child encountered a horse for the first time and called it a 'doggie'. What is the term developed by Jean Piaget for this cognitive process?
questions.explanation: This is an example of assimilation, where the child applies an already existing schema to a new object.

questions.question_text: At which stage of Margaret Mahler's theory of cognitive development does a child perceive his or her mother and self as one unit?
questions.explanation: In the symbiotic stage, the child sees mother and self as a unified whole.

questions.question_text: With what is Lawrence Kohlberg associated?

options.text: Description of the four major stages of morality
Extension of Mary Main's theory of cognitive development in children

questions.explanation: Kohlberg is known for his work on the stages of moral development and moral reasoning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about catharsis is correct?

options.text: It is always necessary to discharge or reduce aggression
Catharsis is most unlikely to be associated with aggression
It is most effective in the management of violent behaviour
It leads to more aggression in patients undergoing catharsis
It is predominantly effective in the long-term management of aggression

correct_answer.text: It leads to more aggression in patients undergoing catharsis

correct_answers.text: It leads to more aggression in patients undergoing catharsis

questions.explanation: While catharsis can provide temporary relief, it may actually increase aggressive behavior in some individuals.

questions.question_text: In which stage of cognitive development, are phenomenalistic causality and animistic thinking are seen?
questions.explanation: Phenomenalistic causality and animistic thinking are characteristic of the preoperational stage.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old woman always felt that she was not as good as her older sister. Which one of Argyle's four dimensions does the above describe?
questions.explanation: Self-esteem refers to how one values oneself in comparison to others.

questions.question_text: Teachers tend to take the credit for a student's academic success but will attribute a student's poor performance to his or her laziness. Which of the following describes the 'fundamental attribution error'? AI chose B

options.text: He failed the examination because he did not have enough time to finish his paper
He failed the examination because he did not study hard enough
He failed the examination due to the ambiguous questions set by the examiners
He passed the examination due to my hard work and academic prowess
He failed the examination because the exam hall was too noisy

correct_answer.text: He passed the examination due to my hard work and academic prowess

correct_answers.text: He passed the examination due to my hard work and academic prowess

questions.explanation: The fundamental attribution error refers to the tendency to overemphasize personal characteristics and downplay situational factors when interpreting others' behaviors.

questions.question_text: French and Raven described the social power derived from the ability to allocate resources. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Reward power is derived from the ability to give benefits or rewards to others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following increases prejudice?

options.text: Stereotyping of the victim of prejudice

correct_answer.text: Stereotyping of the victim of prejudice

correct_answers.text: Stereotyping of the victim of prejudice

questions.explanation: Stereotyping victims reinforces prejudicial attitudes.

questions.question_text: What does the valid test of orientation in a 25-year-old delirious patient include?

options.text: Awareness of the role of the interviewer
Giving correct information about their family

correct_answer.text: Awareness of the role of the interviewer

correct_answers.text: Awareness of the role of the interviewer

questions.explanation: Awareness of the role of the interviewer is a vital component to assess orientation in delirious patients.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the serial sevens test is correct?

options.text: It is a bedside diagnostic test of Alzheimer's disease
It is a good indicator of concentration
It can differentiate cognitive impairment due to a variety of reasons
It is impaired in a psychotic patient
It serves as an indicator of the patient's mathematical ability

correct_answer.text: It is a good indicator of concentration

correct_answers.text: It is a good indicator of concentration

questions.explanation: The serial sevens test assesses attention and concentration, not formal mathematical ability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Kelly's personal construct theory is correct?

options.text: It forms the basis of a therapy that aims to help people construct more effective interpretations and theories of the world
We are unable to develop constructs in order to deal with all kinds of situation or events in later life
We are unable to identify invalid theories that hinder us in later life
We can construct our lives or reconstruct the progress in our lives, following our impulses
We can engage in unconscious mental activities and consequently know about ourselves and the world

correct_answer.text: It forms the basis of a therapy that aims to help people construct more effective interpretations and theories of the world

correct_answers.text: It forms the basis of a therapy that aims to help people construct more effective interpretations and theories of the world

questions.explanation: Kelly's theory emphasizes the importance of personal constructs in shaping how we view the world, guiding therapeutic approaches.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man with alcohol problem undergoes a psychological assessment. He was now willing to accept positive advice for change, make plans for behaviour change, set goals and assess past successes and failures. At which of Prochaska and Diclemente's (1993) stages of behaviour is he at present? AI chose C
questions.explanation: The preparation stage is characterized by individuals making plans and taking small steps towards change.

questions.question_text: A 15-year-old girl told you that she had been repeatedly sexually abused by her stepfather. Which is the first-line management step that you should take?
questions.explanation: The first line of action in cases of abuse is to ensure the safety of the child and refer to social services.

questions.question_text: A 59-year-old man presented complaining bitterly that he had recently been diagnosed with a malignancy. During the assessment, he objected to the statement that he led a healthy lifestyle. Which of the following describes this situation?
questions.explanation: The fallacy of fairness describes an unreasonable expectation of fairness from life events.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old female graduate was assessed for cognitive–behavioural therapy for generalised anxiety disorder. According to the cognitive therapy of anxiety, which of the following is correct?

options.text: Anxiety is a disorder of thinking
Anxiety is associated with physical symptoms

questions.explanation: Catastrophisation involves misinterpreting situations to predict desperately negative outcomes, a significant factor in anxiety.

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old single man had been taking crack cocaine for a few years. He attended a drug advisory centre at the request of his girlfriend. He did not consider this a problem and believed that his girlfriend's worries were excessive. Which of Prochaska and Diclemente's stages of change is reflected here? AI chose B
questions.explanation: In the precontemplation stage, individuals are often unaware of their problematic behavior and not considering change. AI chose D

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about benzodiazepine receptors is correct?

options.text: Benzodiazepine receptors are associated with excitatory neurotransmitters
Chlormethiazole binds to the same site as benzodiazepines
These receptors are linked to sodium channels
Zolpidem binds to a subtype benzodiazepine receptor-1
Zopiclone binds to same site as benzodiazepines

correct_answer.text: These receptors are linked to sodium channels

correct_answers.text: These receptors are linked to sodium channels

questions.explanation: Zolpidem specifically binds to the GABA receptor subtype, benzodiazepine receptor-1, enhancing its effects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about lithium is correct?

options.text: Lithium blood samples are taken 18 hours after the last dose
Only concentrations > 2.0 mmol/L are associated with an increased risk of toxicity
Regular monitoring can lead to poor compliance
Serum lithium concentrations should be measured with changing renal function
Target lithium concentrations range between 0.1 and 0.2 mmol/L

correct_answer.text: Serum lithium concentrations should be measured with changing renal function

correct_answers.text: Serum lithium concentrations should be measured with changing renal function

questions.explanation: Changes in renal function can significantly influence lithium levels, necessitating careful monitoring.

questions.question_text: Pharmacokinetic interactions occur when one drug interferes with the actions of another drug during absorption, distribution and elimination. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Diuretics alter the availability of lithium
Monoamine oxidase inhibitors increase the metabolism of dietary amines
Paracetamol reduces absorption of amitriptyline by about 50%
Valproate is displaced from protein-binding sites by phenytoin

correct_answer.text: Diuretics alter the availability of lithium

correct_answers.text: Diuretics alter the availability of lithium

questions.explanation: Diuretics can significantly impact lithium concentration, affecting its therapeutic levels.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about treatment of depressive illness without psychotic symptoms is correct?

options.text: Antidepressants are effective in 90% of patients
Antidepressants are effective in only 50% of patients
Failure of adequate trials occurs in 25% of patients
Failure of adequate trial of an antidepressant occurs in 15% of patients
Nearly 60% of the partial responders to antidepressants benefit from addition of lithium

correct_answer.text: Failure of adequate trials occurs in 25% of patients

correct_answers.text: Failure of adequate trials occurs in 25% of patients

questions.explanation: Approximately 25% of patients with depressive illness may fail to find relief from antidepressants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the adverse effects of lithium is correct?

options.text: 10–20% of patients show morphological kidney changes with long-term therapy
After 6–18 months of treatment, 60% of women develop hypothyroidism
More than 10% of patients develop irreversible kidney failure after 10 years of treatment
The estimated risk of major congenital abnormalities for lithium-exposed babies is 80%
Up to 70% of patients treated with lithium experience side effects

correct_answer.text: 10–20% of patients show morphological kidney changes with long-term therapy

correct_answers.text: 10–20% of patients show morphological kidney changes with long-term therapy

questions.explanation: Long-term lithium therapy can lead to morphological changes in approximately 10-20% of patients.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the sedative property of tricyclic and tetracyclic antidepressants is correct?

options.text: Amitriptyline is the least sedating tricyclic antidepressant
Desipramine is the most sedating tricyclic antidepressant
Tetracyclic antidepressants have a sedative effect due to anticholinergic properties
Trazodone is a highly sedative tetracyclic antidepressant
Tricyclic antidepressants have a sedative effect due to 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT2) antagonism

correct_answer.text: Trazodone is a highly sedative tetracyclic antidepressant

correct_answers.text: Trazodone is a highly sedative tetracyclic antidepressant

questions.explanation: Trazodone is known for its significant sedative properties among tetracyclic antidepressants.

questions.question_text: A 57-year-old man with hypertension, myocardial infarction and depression received treatment with fluoxetine. However, he developed severe hyponatraemia. Which of the following medications is most suitable in this case for the treatment of depression? AI chose A
questions.explanation: Citalopram is known to have a lower risk of inducing hyponatraemia compared to other SSRIs.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of bipolar depression, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommends the use of quetiapine, provided that it satisfies one of the following criteria. What is that criterion? AI chose A

options.text: An antimanic agent has not been prescribed
An antimanic has already been prescribed
An antipsychotic and antimanic have not been previously tried
An antipsychotic has already been prescribed
An antipsychotic has not been prescribed

correct_answer.text: An antipsychotic has not been prescribed

correct_answers.text: An antipsychotic has not been prescribed

questions.explanation: NICE recommends quetiapine for bipolar depression when no antimanic agent has been used.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of post-stroke depression of a patient who is also taking warfarin, which of the following is the most suitable antidepressant?
questions.explanation: Citalopram has the least interaction with warfarin compared to other SSRIs.

questions.question_text: A 17-year-old man presented to the outpatient clinic with symptoms suggestive of psychosis. He reported having smoked cannabis on a regular basis since a young age. Which of the following statements about cannabis and onset of psychosis is correct?

options.text: Age of onset of psychosis is 2.7 years earlier in cannabis users
Alcohol use is linked with a younger age of onset of psychosis
Cannabis does not influence the age of onset of psychosis
Cannabis users have a delayed onset of psychosis
Cannabis is the only illicit drug linked with an earlier onset of psychosis

correct_answer.text: Age of onset of psychosis is 2.7 years earlier in cannabis users

correct_answers.text: Age of onset of psychosis is 2.7 years earlier in cannabis users

questions.explanation: Evidence shows that cannabis use is associated with an earlier onset of psychotic symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old man has recovered from his first episode of psychosis. His family does not want him to take medication for 'longer than is needed' due to side effects. Which of the following statements about the first 5 years after the onset of a first episode of psychosis is correct? AI chose C

options.text: Most patients who experience a single episode of psychosis never relapse after remission
Up to half of patients who experience a first episode of psychosis relapse within 3 years of remission
Up to half of patients who experience a first episode psychosis relapse within 5 years of remission
Up to 20% of patients who experience a first episode psychosis relapse within 5 years of remission
Up to 80% of patients who experience a first episode psychosis relapse within 5 years of remission

correct_answer.text: Up to 80% of patients who experience a first episode psychosis relapse within 5 years of remission

correct_answers.text: Up to 80% of patients who experience a first episode psychosis relapse within 5 years of remission

questions.explanation: Studies suggest that approximately half of the patients will experience a relapse within five years after the first episode.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about childhood abuse is correct?

options.text: Boys experience more physical abuse than girls
Boys experience more sexual abuse than girls
Fathers are more likely to physically abuse their children
Mothers are more likely to sexually abuse their children
Mothers are as likely as fathers to sexually abuse their children

correct_answer.text: Boys experience more physical abuse than girls

correct_answers.text: Boys experience more physical abuse than girls

questions.explanation: Statistical evidence indicates that boys are more frequently victims of physical abuse than girls.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of sensory deception?

options.text: Perceived irregularity of the shape of an object

questions.explanation: Seeing vivid pictures in clouds is a form of pareidolia, a type of sensory deception.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a sensory distortion?
questions.explanation: Dysmegalopsia refers to a distortion in the perception of size, making it a sensory distortion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about illusions is correct?

options.text: Affect illusions are clinically different from hallucinations
Auditory illusions are the most common modality of illusions
Illusions do not occur in delirium
Pareidolia consists of vivid illusions without any extra effort

correct_answer.text: Pareidolia consists of vivid illusions without any extra effort

correct_answers.text: Pareidolia consists of vivid illusions without any extra effort

questions.explanation: Pareidolia involves seeing familiar patterns, such as faces, in random stimuli, typically without conscious effort.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about hallucinations is correct?

options.text: Charles Bonnet syndrome includes clouding of consciousness
Hallucinations are pathognomonic of psychotic disorders
Hallucinosis is a characteristic feature of alcohol intoxication
Lesions of the diencephalon can lead to auditory hallucinations
Normal people can be persuaded to hallucinate

correct_answer.text: Normal people can be persuaded to hallucinate

correct_answers.text: Normal people can be persuaded to hallucinate

questions.explanation: Studies have shown that under specific conditions, even non-psychotic individuals can be induced to experience hallucinations.

questions.question_text: A 24-year-old man smelt burning rubber when he saw red signal at traffic lights and was convinced of the link between them. What is this phenomenon known as?
questions.explanation: Reflex hallucination refers to sensory experience triggered by an external stimulus, suggesting a link that is not present.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man has been diagnosed as having locked-in syndrome. Which of the following statements is correct? AI chose B

options.text: It is caused by a lesion in motor pathways in the dorsal pons
It is characterised by akinetic mutism
Joints in the arms and legs get locked, leading to rigidity

correct_answer.text: It is characterised by akinetic mutism

correct_answers.text: It is characterised by akinetic mutism

questions.explanation: Locked-in syndrome usually results from lesions in the ventral pons affecting motor pathways while sparing consciousness.

questions.question_text: A 69-year-old woman was found wandering in the streets. She was disoriented on assessment in the accident and emergency department. Which of the following statements about orientation is correct?

options.text: Disorientation rules out a functional psychiatric illness
Established disorientation in time and place requires clouding of consciousness
Hysterical dissociation is present with apparent disorientation
Loss of the knowledge of the patient's own name and identity occurs before the disorientation of others' identity
Orientation in space is disturbed before orientation in time

correct_answer.text: Hysterical dissociation is present with apparent disorientation

correct_answers.text: Hysterical dissociation is present with apparent disorientation

questions.explanation: Hysterical dissociation can present with apparent disorientation, emphasizing the complexity of orientation issues.

questions.question_text: A 52-year-old man with a long history of alcohol dependence and memory problems presents with confabulation. Which one of the following is correct with regard to confabulation? AI chose B

options.text: Memory of actual events displaced in space or time
False memory syndrome as the memory is impaired

correct_answer.text: Memory of actual events displaced in space or time

correct_answers.text: Memory of actual events displaced in space or time

questions.explanation: Confabulation is a classic feature of Korsakoff's syndrome, where the patient generates fabricated memories.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is pathognomonic of organic brain disease?
questions.explanation: Perseveration can be a distinct indicator related to organic brain damage.

questions.question_text: A 24-year-old man suddenly collapsed on hearing the news of his country winning the world cup. What is the most likely phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Cataplexy is characterized by sudden loss of muscle tone, often triggered by strong emotions.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old man saw a car flashing its indicator to turn right and immediately believed that he was the heir to the throne. What is this phenomenon called? AI chose A
questions.explanation: Delusions of grandeur involve an inflated sense of self-importance or special status.

questions.question_text: A 26-year-old woman believed that she was the owner of the Manchester United Football Club. Which of the following dimensions best describes the severity of the delusion? AI chose A
questions.explanation: The content dimension refers to the specific beliefs encompassed in a delusion, like ownership.

questions.question_text: A patient says 'I am well today-ay-ay-ay-ay…'. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: Logoclonia involves the repetition of syllables, often occurring in neurological conditions.

questions.question_text: You administered the MMSE to a 65-year-old man. On asking about the day of the week, he said 'Monday'. Then you asked him about the month and he still said 'Monday'. When you asked him about the year, he told you 'Monday'. What is this best described as?
questions.explanation: Perseveration occurs when a response continues beyond its relevance, indicated by the repeated 'Monday' responses.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of depersonalisation?

options.text: Affect can be pleasant in some cases
It is clearly distinguishable from derealisation

questions.explanation: Depersonalisation is defined as a subjective experience where individuals feel detached from themselves.

questions.question_text: What does the 'serial sevens' test assess?
questions.explanation: The serial sevens test primarily assesses concentration and mental arithmetic.

questions.question_text: A doctor, when carrying out a physical examination of the cardiovascular system on a female patient, asked her to unbutton her 'skirt' instead of her 'shirt'. What is this described as?
questions.explanation: Parapraxis, or a Freudian slip, occurs when a mistake reveals unconscious thoughts.

questions.question_text: What is Broca's dysphasia characterised by?
questions.explanation: Broca's dysphasia is characterized by telegraphic speech, where speech is non-fluent and lacks grammatical structure.

questions.question_text: Which of following is not an extreme form of cooperation?
questions.explanation: Advertence is not classified as a form of cooperation or compliance

questions.question_text: What is familiarity with an unfamiliar situation called?
questions.explanation: Jamais-vu describes the feeling of unfamiliarity in a familiar situation, the opposite of déjà-vu.

questions.question_text: Which of the following explains memory impairment accurately?

options.text: Following a cerebral trauma, retrograde amnesia occurs due to problems in registration
In Korsakoff's syndrome, memory impairment occurs due to a problem in recall
Memory impairment due to electroconvulsive therapy includes apparent loss of memory stores
Memory stays intact in a fugue state
Confabulation is an example of a problem with 'retention'

correct_answer.text: Memory impairment due to electroconvulsive therapy includes apparent loss of memory stores

correct_answers.text: Memory impairment due to electroconvulsive therapy includes apparent loss of memory stores

questions.explanation: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is most likely to impair memories of events immediately preceding   the treatment, particularly more recent autobiographical memories. Memory impairment due to   ECT includes impaired learning ability, defective retrieval and apparent loss of memory stores. In   some cases, anterograde amnesia can also occur. In Korsakoff’s syndrome, anterograde amnesia   occurs due to problems at registration (encoding). Retrograde amnesia occurs after cerebral trauma   due to impairment of retention (storage). Recognition is the retrieval of stored information which   depends on the identification of items previously learned. Recall is the effortful retrieval of stored   information. Confabulation is due to problems in retrieval. Registration can be impaired in fugue.

questions.question_text: According to the Kübler–Ross model, which of the following constitutes one of the stages of grief?
questions.explanation: Anger is one of the recognized stages of grief in the Kübler-Ross model.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man believed that this world was a dirty place to live in. He washed his hands several times and took a bath twice a day. He drank only bottled water, washed his clothes in hot water with a particular detergent, got medically examined every 6 months and stayed away from pets. He does not think that there is anything wrong in such thinking. Which of the following describes the psychopathology?
questions.explanation: The behaviors indicate both obsession (intrusive thoughts) and compulsion (ritualistic cleaning).

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old medical student, confronted with an enormous mass of information and responsibility, became engrossed in her work, and felt less anxious and mentally stronger for continuing her studies. Which of the following coping mechanisms can explain the situation?
questions.explanation: Mastery and control refers to actively engaging with stressors to improve psychological well-being.

questions.question_text: During an individual psychotherapy session, the therapist began talking excessively and confronted the patient. This was probably a result of something in the patient's behaviour and his interaction with the therapist. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: Countertransference refers to the therapist's emotional reactions influenced by the patient's behavior.

questions.question_text: Who was associated with replacing 'dementia praecox' by the term 'schizophrenia'?
questions.explanation: Eugen Bleuler is credited with introducing the term schizophrenia, shifting away from the earlier concept of dementia praecox.

questions.question_text: Who was responsible for translating 'démence précoce' into 'dementia praecox'?
questions.explanation: Kraepelin translated 'démence précoce' into 'dementia praecox', reflecting his diagnostic approach.

questions.question_text: Who coined the term 'démence précoce'?
questions.explanation: Benedict Morel was the first to use the term 'démence précoce' to describe early-onset mental illness.

questions.question_text: In 1983, Raven developed Raven's progressive matrices test to overcome which of the following limitations of previous tests?
questions.explanation: Raven's matrices were designed to eliminate cultural and language biases in IQ testing.

questions.question_text: What does Plutchik's wheel represent?
questions.explanation: Plutchik's wheel is a model of emotions, illustrating primary emotions and their relationships.

questions.question_text: Who is associated with the concept of 'good-enough mothers'?
questions.explanation: Donald Winnicott introduced the idea of 'good-enough mothers' to describe responsive yet imperfect caregiving.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Freud's 'interpretation of dreams' is correct?

options.text: Dream work is the process by which unconscious wishes are processed into dreams
Secondary revision refers to dreams that recur time and again
Dreams are manifestations of unconscious fears
The manifest content is not accessible to the dreamer
The latent content of the dreams refers to the meaning behind them

correct_answer.text: Dream work is the process by which unconscious wishes are processed into dreams

correct_answers.text: Dream work is the process by which unconscious wishes are processed into dreams

questions.explanation: The latent content of dreams represents the underlying meaning of the dream as interpreted by Freud.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is credited to Benedict Morel?

options.text: Described schizophrenia in people with an 'asthenic' body type
Differentiated patients with schizophrenia and manic–depressive psychosis

questions.explanation: Benedict Morel is known for coining the term 'démence précoce' in his work related to schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the findings of the International pilot study of schizophrenia is correct?

options.text: Catatonic symptoms were frequent among patients in developing countries
Delusions and hallucinations were more frequent in western populations
Standardised assessment and diagnostic measures were not applicable to all populations
The core symptoms of schizophrenia varied across cultures
Two-year outcome was better in developed centres

correct_answer.text: Catatonic symptoms were frequent among patients in developing countries

correct_answers.text: Catatonic symptoms were frequent among patients in developing countries

questions.explanation: The study found that catatonic symptoms were indeed more frequently observed among patients from developing countries.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the cultural phenomenon of psychosis is correct?

options.text: At the 2-year follow-up, patients from developed countries were better
Incidence of core schizophrenia showed a three-fold difference across centres
Psychotic experiences in mania are more common in Europeans than African–Caribbean patients
The broad diagnosis of schizophrenia (lacking schneiderian symptoms) showed a three-fold difference across countries
The incidence of mania is the same in ethnic minorities living in developed countries as that of their native populations

correct_answer.text: The incidence of mania is the same in ethnic minorities living in developed countries as that of their native populations

correct_answers.text: The incidence of mania is the same in ethnic minorities living in developed countries as that of their native populations

questions.explanation: The core symptoms of schizophrenia varied across cultures, showing significant differences in incidence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the strange situation procedure is correct?

options.text: Sixty-five percent of infants securely are attached by 12 months
Assessment can be done in adolescence
This procedure was developed by Winnicott
The infant is exposed to escalating amounts of stress

correct_answer.text: The infant is exposed to escalating amounts of stress

correct_answers.text: The infant is exposed to escalating amounts of stress

questions.explanation: The strange situation exposes infants to escalating levels of stress to assess attachment behavior.
